cd /Users/mike/github/sw-ml-study/demo-extensions
python3 - <<'PY'
p='docs/network-db-extensions.md'; s=open(p).read()
old='''## Bounded large-artifact download (core delivered, surface pending)'''
new='''## Bounded large-artifact download'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
old2='''`download_value` in `extensions/http-client/src/download.rs` streams one
artifact of declared length and SHA-256 digest into a confined path beneath an
explicit root. The pure rules live in `download_plan.rs` and never touch the
network or filesystem; the effects module owns confinement, verified reuse,
streamed hashing, and atomic publication. The native `_http:download`
registration, MLPL facade, and `just fetch-artifact` recipe follow in the next
saga step (`docs/reasoning-extensions-saga.md`).'''
new2='''`_http:download(record)` streams one artifact of declared length and SHA-256
digest into a confined path beneath an explicit root. The pure rules live in
`extensions/http-client/src/download_plan.rs` and never touch the network or
filesystem; `download.rs` owns confinement, verified reuse, streamed hashing,
and atomic publication.

The public MLPL facade is `u:http_download(url, expected_bytes, sha256, root,
path, chunk_bytes, timeout_ms)` in `extensions/http-client/module.mlpl`, with
`u:http_download_request(...)` building the record alone for tests that must
not transfer anything. Ownership split: Rust performs one generic
checksum-verified transfer into a confined path and knows nothing about models,
vocabularies, or artifact names; MLPL chooses the URL, the pinned size and
digest, the cache layout, and what to do with the outcome.'''
assert old2 in s; s=s.replace(old2,new2,1)

old3='''Evidence: `extensions/http-client/tests/download_contract.rs` proves success,'''
new3='''### Error taxonomy

Invalid-argument errors are raised before any I/O: a malformed or non-exact
record, a non-HTTP(S) URL, a relative or missing root, an unconfined or empty
path, an out-of-range length, chunk, or timeout, and a digest that is not 64
hexadecimal characters. A path whose parent or existing target resolves outside
the canonical root, or that names a directory, is also an invalid argument.

Extension errors describe a transfer that was attempted and refused: a
non-2xx status, a transport failure (including an exhausted redirect budget), a
`Content-Length` that disagrees with `expected_bytes`, a truncated or
over-delivered body, a digest mismatch, and filesystem failures while writing,
flushing, or publishing. All of them leave no file at the target.

A successful extension call yields a bare record to MLPL while a failure yields
an err result, so neither `is_ok` nor field access is total across both. The
demo classifies the outcome with `type_of` and `str_eq`; the underlying host
asymmetry is filed as R1 in `sw-mlpl-requests.md`.

### Running it

`just fetch-artifact URL EXPECTED_BYTES SHA256 RELATIVE_PATH [ROOT]` runs
`demos/http-client/download.mlpl` through the upstream host binary. `ROOT`
defaults to `models/`, which is git-ignored because a pinned artifact is a
downloaded product and never source.

The first artifacts this exists for are published by Hugging Face:

| Artifact | Bytes |
|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base/tokenizer.json` | 7,031,645 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base/model.safetensors` | 1,192,135,096 |

Their SHA-256 digests are not vendored here. Take each digest from the
publisher, pass it explicitly, and the transfer either matches it or leaves
nothing behind. This command performs real network I/O and is opt-in; no gate
or test requires it.

Evidence: `extensions/http-client/tests/download_contract.rs` proves success,'''
assert old3 in s; s=s.replace(old3,new3,1)

old4='''digests, and pre-I/O rejection of unsafe inputs using loopback listeners only.'''
new4='''digests, and pre-I/O rejection of unsafe inputs using loopback listeners only.
`extensions/http-client/tests/provider_contract.rs` pins the registered name,
help text, and argument rejection across the dynamic and static providers, and
`tests/test_http_module.mlpl` pins the facade record shape without transferring
anything. The facade itself was exercised end to end against a local server on
2026-09-17: a 200,000-byte payload published with its expected digest, a second
run reported `reused: 1` with the server still running, and a tampered digest,
a size mismatch, and a `../` path each failed with a distinct message leaving
zero files under the root.'''
assert old4 in s; s=s.replace(old4,new4,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
echo OK; grep -n 'fetch-artifact\|reused: 1' docs/network-db-extensions.md | head

content.text:
The gate is running. Step 002 is functionally complete and verified end to end against a local server.

What I built:

- **`_http:download` registered** through the SDK, with matching help text pinned in the dynamic and static provider contract test.
- **MLPL facade** `u:http_download` plus `u:http_download_request`, which builds the record alone so the mlplunit test pins the shape without transferring anything.
- **`just fetch-artifact`** backed by a script and a new demo source, running through the upstream host binary.
- **`models/` is git-ignored**, since a pinned artifact is a downloaded product, not source.

Live verification against a local server, all in one run:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| First fetch | published with expected digest, `reused: 0` |
| Second fetch | `reused: 1`, no connection opened |
| Tampered digest | digest mismatch, zero files left |
| Size mismatch | content-length disagreement, zero files left |
| `../` path | rejected as unconfined |

**Two host findings filed rather than worked around silently**, per your instruction. Extension calls return a bare value on success but a result value on failure, so neither `is_ok` nor field access is total across both outcomes. That is R1 in the sw-mlpl requests document. R2 records that `get_error` fails on a string payload where `err_message` works. Neither blocks the saga; the demo classifies the outcome with `type_of` and the workaround is documented.

I did not vendor the Qwen3 digests. The sizes are published in the work order, but the digests are not, so the recipe takes the digest explicitly from the publisher rather than inviting me to invent one.

Step 002 is complete, pushed, and work order E2 is finished. Per the agentrail protocol I stop here rather than starting step 003.

**What shipped.** The bounded download is now reachable from MLPL as `u:http_download`, with a record-builder variant so tests can pin the shape without transferring anything. **Verified live against a local server**, all five paths:

| Case | Outcome |
|---|---|
| First fetch | published, digest matched, `reused: 0` |
| Second fetch | `reused: 1`, no connection opened |
| Tampered digest | rejected, zero files left |
| Size mismatch | rejected before writing, zero files left |
| `../` path | rejected as unconfined |

The full gate passed with `PASS pre-commit`, covering 21 crate tests and 112 MLPL tests. No gate step invokes the fetch recipe, so nothing in the gate depends on the public network.

**Two host findings filed instead of papered over**, following your instruction to record upstream needs. The first is that an extension call returns a bare value on success but a result value on failure, so neither `is_ok` nor field access works across both outcomes. I found this by running the demo and then probing the interpreter for a total idiom, landing on `type_of` with `str_eq`. The second records that `get_error` fails on a string payload where `err_message` works. Both are in the sw-mlpl requests document; neither blocks the saga, though the first will matter more for the tokenizer facade in steps 5 and 6.

**One judgment call.** The work order publishes the Qwen3 byte sizes but not their SHA-256 digests. Rather than invent or guess a digest, the recipe takes it from the publisher as an explicit argument, so a wrong digest simply leaves nothing behind.

The gate caught one thing I missed: a rustfmt diff in the new host binary. Fixed before the commit landed.

Next is step 003, which writes the tokenizer extension contract document and the synthetic Hugging Face fixture.

#!/bin/sh
# Download the MATH-500 evaluation set (JSONL) into the ignored data/ tree.
# Opt-in: never part of `just check`. Prints provenance, checks the published
# byte size, and refuses to overwrite an existing file.
set -eu

repo_root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
url="https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500/resolve/main/test.jsonl"
expected_bytes=446564
dest="$repo_root/data/math500/test.jsonl"

echo "MATH-500 evaluation set"
echo "  source:  $url"
echo "  origin:  OpenAI PRM800K MATH splits (https://github.com/openai/prm800k), 500 problems"
echo "  license: per the dataset card; the PRM800K source repository is MIT licensed"
echo "  dest:    ${dest#"$repo_root/"} (ignored by git, never redistributed)"

if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
    echo "refusing to overwrite existing file: ${dest#"$repo_root/"}" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
tmp="$dest.part"
curl -L --fail --silent --show-error -o "$tmp" "$url"
actual=$(wc -c < "$tmp" | tr -d ' ')
if [ "$actual" -ne "$expected_bytes" ]; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    echo "size mismatch: expected $expected_bytes bytes, got $actual; refusing the download" >&2
    exit 1
fi
mv "$tmp" "$dest"
echo "  bytes:   $actual (matches the published size)"

content.text:
No, I'm not, and you've found a real gap. Here's the accurate state.

**Neither repository holds a single SHA-256 value.** I searched the downstream repo: no digest appears anywhere in its scripts or docs. Its two fetch scripts use `curl` and verify byte size only. My download path requires a caller-supplied digest, and I deliberately did not invent one.

**What that does and does not block:**

- It does not block this saga. Steps 3 through 8 build the tokenizer extension and need no digests.
- It does block the downstream switchover. Their `feature-homes.md` says the fetch recipes move from `curl` to the extension once it can stream to a checksum-verified file. It can now, but they have nothing to pass as the digest, so they cannot actually make that switch.

**I also overstated E2 slightly.** I reported the work order complete. The mechanism is complete and proven against a local server across five paths. The acceptance sentence names a checksum-verified file appearing for the two specific Qwen3 artifacts, and that has never run against the real artifacts because no digest exists for them.

**This is cheap to resolve.** Hugging Face stores large files through Git LFS, and the pointer file carries the digest. Requesting the raw pointer for `model.safetensors` returns its SHA-256 in a few hundred bytes, with no need to transfer 1.19 GB. The same works for `tokenizer.json` and the MATH-500 set.

Two things I'd do, and I want your call before touching an external service or a sibling repository:

1. Fetch the three LFS pointers, record the digests in the download documentation as pinned provenance, and run the real end-to-end acceptance for `tokenizer.json`, which is only 7 MB.
2. Write the gap down. There is no `docs/reasoning-from-scratch-requests.md`, and the digest question belongs to whoever pins the artifacts. Right now it is recorded nowhere, which is how it stayed invisible until you asked.

Say the word and I'll do both, or just the write-up if you'd rather keep network access out of it.

Understood, no changes to sibling repos. Here's what I found before acting on it.

**No SHA-256 request exists anywhere.** The downstream repo's requests to sw-mlpl run R1 through R9 and none concerns hashing. Their requests to this repo list E1, E2, E3 and none is a digest primitive. So the request you're asking about has never been written down, by anyone.

**You're right that it can't live in MLPL.** SHA-256 is 64 rounds of 32-bit modular addition, rotation and xor per 64-byte block. For the 1.19 GB weights that is roughly 18.6 million blocks, so on the order of a billion round operations, and MLPL has no native 32-bit integer type to do them in. That is not a slow implementation, it's an infeasible one.

**And it belongs here, not upstream.** It needs no differentiation, it is byte-level and throughput-bound, and every other ecosystem ships it in a standard library. That is exactly this repository's criterion for a Rust extension. So this is my work, not something I document for another agent.

I'm adding it to the saga now, ahead of the tokenizer work, since downstream is blocked on it.

Insert a new pending step at a chosen position, shifting later steps up

Use when a bug or unplanned task needs to slot in before existing pending work. The new step lands at position `after + 1`; every pending/in-progress step with a number greater than `after` shifts up by one (step.toml `number` and the on-disk `NNN-slug` directory name are both updated). The operation is refused if any step that would shift is already `Completed`, since completed steps anchor git-tracked history.

Pass `--after 0` to prepend at position 1 (only works if step 1 is pending).

Cursor semantic (preemption): if the new step lands at or before the current cursor, focus follows the new arrival — the inserted step becomes `current_step` and the previously focused step is pushed to `current_step + 1`. This matches the "drop in a blocker" use case. If the new step lands behind the cursor, focus is unchanged and the new step is queued as future work.

14	fn record(fields: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'static str, Value)>) -> Value {
15	    Value::Record(
16	        fields
17	            .into_iter()
18	            .map(|(name, value)| (name.to_owned(), value))
19	            .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>(),
20	    )
21	}
22	
23	fn file_request(root: &Path, path: &str, chunk_bytes: i64) -> Value {
24	    record([
25	        ("root", Value::String(root.to_str().unwrap().to_owned())),
26	        ("path", Value::String(path.to_owned())),
27	        ("chunk_bytes", Value::I64(chunk_bytes)),
28	    ])
29	}
30	
31	fn digest_of(value: Value) -> String {
32	    match sha256_bytes_value(&[value]).unwrap() {
33	        Value::String(digest) => digest,
34	        other => panic!("expected a string digest, got {other:?}"),
35	    }
36	}
37	
38	fn field<'a>(value: &'a Value, name: &str) -> &'a Value {
39	    let Value::Record(fields) = value else {
40	        panic!("result must be a record");
41	    };
42	    fields.get(name).unwrap()
43	}

47	    assert_eq!(digest_of(Value::Bytes(b"abc".to_vec())), ABC);

50	            b"abcdbcdecdefdefgefghfghighijhijkijkljklmklmnlmnomnopnopq".to_vec()
51	        )),
52	        ABC_LONG
53	    );
54	    assert_eq!(digest_of(Value::Bytes(Vec::new())), EMPTY);
55	}

59	    assert!(

61	            .unwrap_err()
62	            .message()
63	            .contains("must be bytes")
64	    );
65	    assert!(
66	        sha256_bytes_value(&[])
67	            .unwrap_err()

70	    );
71	}

73	#[test]
74	fn file_digest_matches_the_in_memory_digest_at_every_chunk_size() {
75	    let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
76	    // 4096 + 1 bytes, so a power-of-two chunk never aligns with the end.
77	    let body = (0..4097)
78	        .map(|index| u8::try_from((index * 31 + 7) % 256).unwrap())
79	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
80	    fs::create_dir_all(root.path().join("vendor")).unwrap();
81	    fs::write(root.path().join("vendor/blob.bin"), &body).unwrap();
82	    let expected = digest_of(Value::Bytes(body.clone()));
83	
84	    // 1 byte forces the single-byte path; 64 and 4096 straddle the SHA-256
85	    // block size; 1 MiB reads the file in one call.
86	    for chunk in [1, 64, 4096, 1024 * 1024] {

95	    }
96	}

input.content:
# Content-digest extension (`_digest`)

A generic SHA-256 primitive. It hashes bytes; it knows nothing about models,
vocabularies, artifact names, or why a caller wants a digest.

## Why this is native

SHA-256 compresses each 64-byte block through 64 rounds of 32-bit modular
addition, bitwise rotation, and exclusive-or. The 1.19 GB artifact this
repository's consumers pin is roughly 18.6 million blocks, so about 1.2 billion
round operations.

MLPL has no native 32-bit integer type. Expressing the rounds means emulating
`u32` wrap-around, rotation, and xor on f64 arrays, which multiplies both the
operation count and the memory traffic. The result would not be a slow
implementation of a fast algorithm; it would be an impractical one, and the
digest of a gigabyte artifact would never finish in a teaching demo.

By this repository's own rule in `../reasoning-from-scratch/docs/feature-homes.md`,
that makes it extension work: no differentiation, byte-level, throughput-bound,
and shipped in a standard library everywhere else.

## Surface

Private namespace `_digest`, public facade `digest` in
`extensions/digest/module.mlpl`.

| Call | Returns |
|---|---|
| `_digest:sha256_bytes(bytes)` | lowercase hexadecimal digest string |
| `_digest:sha256_file({root, path, chunk_bytes})` | record with `sha256` and `bytes` |

`u:digest_sha256_bytes(bytes)` and `u:digest_sha256_file(root, path,
chunk_bytes)` are the public facade calls, with
`u:digest_sha256_file_request(...)` building the record alone so tests can pin
its shape without reading anything.

`sha256_file` confines exactly as the SQLite and download surfaces do: `root`
must be an absolute existing directory, `path` a non-empty relative path whose
components are all normal, and the canonical target must still resolve beneath
the canonical root. A symbolic link pointing outside the root is rejected after
canonicalization, not before. `chunk_bytes` runs from 1 to 16 MiB and bounds
resident memory, so hashing a gigabyte file never loads a gigabyte.

## Error taxonomy

Invalid-argument errors, raised before any read: a non-record or non-exact
record, a non-bytes argument to `sha256_bytes`, a relative or missing root, an
empty, absolute, or traversing path, a path that escapes the root or does not
name a regular file, and an out-of-range `chunk_bytes`. Extension errors cover
a file that cannot be opened or read. Nothing panics.

## One hashing implementation

`Sha256Stream` in `extensions/digest/src/sha256.rs` is the only SHA-256
implementation in the repository, including its hexadecimal rendering. The
bounded download in `http-client` drives that type directly from its own read
loop, because it must also enforce a byte limit and tee each chunk into a
temporary file. Transfer policy stays in the download; hashing stays here.

## Evidence

`extensions/digest/tests/digest_contract.rs` checks the published NIST
one-block and two-block vectors and the empty-input vector, agreement between
the in-memory and streamed file digests at chunk sizes of 1, 64, 4096, and
1 MiB over a 4,097-byte input whose length is deliberately not a multiple of
any of them, an empty file, symbolic-link escape, and every fail-closed input.
`extensions/digest/tests/provider_contract.rs` pins the registered names, help
text, and argument rejection across the dynamic and static providers.
`tests/test_digest_module.mlpl` pins the facade record shape.

## What this unblocks

Consumers that pin an artifact by digest can now compute and verify one without
the algorithm in MLPL. `../reasoning-from-scratch` currently verifies its
downloads by byte size alone; a size check detects truncation but not
substitution. With this primitive its fetch recipes can pin a real digest, and
`u:http_download` can consume it.

Neither this repository nor its consumers hold published SHA-256 values for the
Qwen3 artifacts yet. Obtaining and pinning them is the consumer's decision and
belongs in that repository, not here.

# Requests to `../reasoning-from-scratch`

Changes this repository needs from its downstream consumer. Nothing here is
implemented from this repository; each entry is a work order for that
repository's agent, who revalidates it before acting. This file exists because
work orders flow both ways: that repository's asks of this one live in its
`docs/demo-extensions-requests.md`.

## D1. Pin artifact digests, now that a SHA-256 primitive exists

Raised by: step `003-digest-primitive` (2026-09-18).

`scripts/fetch-math500` and `scripts/fetch-model` verify a download by
published byte size alone. A size check detects a truncated transfer but not a
substituted one: any replacement of the same length passes.

Two capabilities now exist here to close that gap:

- `_digest:sha256_bytes` / `_digest:sha256_file` compute a digest natively,
  streaming a file in bounded chunks. See `digest-extension.md`. This exists
  because SHA-256 is impractical to implement in MLPL, which has no 32-bit
  integer type for its rounds.
- `_http:download` streams a transfer into a temporary file under a granted
  root, verifies a declared length and SHA-256, and only then renames it into
  place. See `network-db-extensions.md`.

Requested: obtain the published SHA-256 for each pinned artifact, record it
alongside the byte size already recorded, and verify against it. The artifacts
named in `demo-extensions-requests.md` E2 are
`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base/tokenizer.json` (7,031,645 bytes) and
`model.safetensors` (1,192,135,096 bytes); `MATH-500/test.jsonl` (446,564
bytes) has the same gap.

Note for whoever does this: Hugging Face serves large files through Git LFS,
and the LFS pointer carries the SHA-256. Requesting the raw pointer rather than
the resolved file yields the digest in a few hundred bytes, with no need to
transfer 1.19 GB to learn it.

Why this is not done here: the digests are provenance for artifacts that
repository pins, licenses, and documents. Choosing and recording them is its
decision, and this repository does not modify sibling repositories.

Status: open. It does not block any step of the active saga here.
EOF

from here.''','''Any change needed in a sibling repository is recorded here as a work order for
that repository's agent, in `docs/sw-mlpl-requests.md`,
`docs/demo-mlpl-libraries-requests.md`, or
`docs/reasoning-from-scratch-requests.md`. No sibling repository is modified
from here.''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='README.md'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('extensions/http-client/         Bounded HTTP/HTTPS, verified large download, and middleware policy',

open(p,'w').write(s)

content.text:
The gate is running. Summary of the digest work while it completes.

**Your framing was right, and it exposed a real hole in what I'd shipped.** I delivered checksum verification in step 002 that no consumer could actually use, because computing the digest was left to them and they have no way to compute one. A verification mechanism whose input nobody can produce is not finished work.

**Why it cannot live in MLPL**, which is the point you made: SHA-256 runs 64 rounds of 32-bit modular addition, rotation and xor per 64-byte block. The 1.19 GB artifact is about 18.6 million blocks. MLPL has no 32-bit integer type, so every round would be emulated on f64 arrays. That is not slow, it is impractical.

**What I built.** A small `extensions/digest` crate with `_digest:sha256_bytes` for in-memory data and `_digest:sha256_file` for streaming an existing confined file in bounded chunks, so hashing a gigabyte never loads a gigabyte. It reuses the same root-confinement rules as the SQLite and download surfaces, and rejects a symlink that escapes the root after canonicalization.

**One hashing implementation, as the step required.** I exposed a `Sha256Stream` type and had the download drive it from its own read loop, since the download additionally enforces a byte limit and tees each chunk to a temporary file. Transfer policy stays in the download, hashing stays in the digest crate. Six digest tests, thirteen download tests, and 113 MLPL tests pass.

**Recorded, not implemented, for the other repo.** The downstream fetch scripts verify by byte size alone, which catches truncation but not substitution. I wrote that up as request D1 in a new requests document for their agent, including the detail that Hugging Face exposes the digest in the LFS pointer, so nobody needs to transfer 1.19 GB to learn it. Choosing and pinning those digests is their call, and I did not touch their repo.

git add -A extensions/digest docs tests scripts Cargo.toml Cargo.lock README.md extensions/http-client .agentrail
git status --short | grep -v '^[MAR] ' | head
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(digest): add a native streaming SHA-256 primitive

Add extensions/digest exposing _digest:sha256_bytes(bytes) for in-memory data
and _digest:sha256_file({root, path, chunk_bytes}) for streaming an existing
confined file, with the u:digest_* MLPL facade.

Why this exists: step 002 delivered checksum-verified downloads, but a consumer
that cannot compute a digest cannot use that verification. SHA-256 is 64 rounds
of 32-bit modular addition, rotation, and exclusive-or per 64-byte block, so
the 1.19 GB artifact downstream pins is roughly 18.6 million blocks. MLPL has
no 32-bit integer type, so every round would be emulated on f64 arrays. That is
not a slow implementation of the algorithm, it is an impractical one. No
differentiation, byte-level, throughput-bound: extension work by this
repository's own rule.

Confinement matches the SQLite and download surfaces: absolute existing root,
non-empty relative path of normal components, canonical target still beneath
the canonical root, so a symlink pointing outside is rejected after resolution.
chunk_bytes runs from 1 to 16 MiB and bounds resident memory, so hashing a
gigabyte file never loads a gigabyte.

One hashing implementation: Sha256Stream is the only SHA-256 in the repository,
including its hexadecimal rendering. The bounded download drives that type from
its own read loop because it must additionally enforce a byte limit and tee
each chunk into a temporary file; transfer policy stays in the download and
hashing stays here. http-client keeps sha2 only as a dev-dependency for
computing test expectations.

Tests: published NIST one-block and two-block vectors plus the empty-input
vector; agreement between the in-memory and streamed digests at chunk sizes of
1, 64, 4096, and 1 MiB over a 4,097-byte input whose length is a multiple of
none of them; an empty file; symlink escape; every fail-closed input; and
dynamic/static provider parity for names, help text, and argument rejection.

Record request D1 in the new docs/reasoning-from-scratch-requests.md: that
repository verifies downloads by published byte size alone, which detects
truncation but not substitution, and can now pin real digests. Obtaining them
is its decision; no sibling repository is modified from here.

Validation: cargo test -p mlpl-extension-digest -p mlpl-extension-http-client
(6 digest, 13 download, and provider tests passing); scripts/run-tests (113
MLPL tests passing); scripts/check (full gate, PASS pre-commit).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
